chunks: And he was asked about a house that had been a latrine for some time: is it suitable for it to be made into a mosque?
So he said: "If it is cleaned and repaired, then there is no harm."

key_terms.أُصْلِحَ: was repaired or restored to proper condition
key_terms.بَيْتٍ: a house or structure under discussion
key_terms.حَشًّا: a latrine or place used for relieving oneself
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.مَسْجِدًا: a mosque; a place designated for worship and sajdah (prostration)
key_terms.نُظِّفَ: was cleaned and purified from filth
key_terms.يَصْلُحُ: is suitable or valid for the intended use

ai.seo_question: Can a place that was formerly used as a latrine be turned into a mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a place formerly used as a latrine. It indicates that if such a place is properly cleaned and restored, there is no objection to making it into a mosque.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.711 - Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal, Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) was asked about a house that had been used as a latrine for a period of time and whether it would be suitable to make it into a mosque.
Imam (as) said: "If it is cleaned and repaired, then there is no harm."
